newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria opposition says Commonwealth visit failed.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria opposition says Commonwealth visit failed.

text.p: The Nigerian umbrella opposition NADECO group on Tuesday condemned as a failure a Commonwealth mission to Nigeria to pressure the country to respect human rights and restore democracy more quickly.
"The CMAG (Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group) mission has failed and is clearly designed to affirm the status quo," NADECO said in an open letter to the Commonwealth secretariat in London.
CMAG, made up the foreign ministers of eight Commonwealth nations was in Nigeria for two days of talks last week during which they met only government representatives.
During the visit Nigeria also released three leading opposition activists detained since early this year.

"It would seem that CMAG, contrary to what we had hoped, eventually succumbed to the various impediments and obstacles placed in its way by the Nigerian government to frustrate its mission," said NADECO.
CMAG was set up at the last Commonwealth summit in Auckland, New Zealand, where Nigeria was suspended for hanging nine minority rights activists including writer Ken Saro-Wiwa.

CMAG chairman and Zimbabwean Foreign Minister Stan Mudenge told a news conference at the end of the visit that Nigerian ruler General Sani Abacha gave them permission to meet anyone they wanted but time constraints prevented them doing so.
CMAG is made up of Britain, Canada, New Zealand, South Africa, Zimbabwe, Ghana, Jamaica and Malaysia and its report will be submitted to the Commonwealth secretariat in London.
Nigeria, Africa's most populous nation, plunged into political turmoil in June 1993 when the army annulled a presidential election in spite of pledges to restore democracy.
Among many people still in detention are Moshood Abiola, the wealthy businessman presumed to have won the annulled poll.
Abacha has promised to hand over to a democratically-elected president in 1998, a promise critics are sceptical about.
NADECO said the outcome of the CMAG visit did not augur well for genuine democracy in Nigeria.

"The endorsement of political manipulation can only carry grave consequences for the future of Nigeria and the West African sub region," said the NADECO letter, addressed to Commonwealth secretary general Emeka Anyaoku, a Nigerian.
